description: ODC (coverage T): NESTED STRUCTURE, STRUCTURE LIST INSIDE A STRUCTURE and STRUCTURE AS A PARAMETER - the shape that consumed REST and exposed REST produce and consume, and that structure-list-type.json did not cover yet (there the structure list belonged only to a variable and to an output). It mirrors tests/jobs/spec-data.json (a single spec op declares the composite types) and tests/jobs/rest-query-nested.json (nesting read by path: Address.Geo.Latitude). Three levels: WfCovPolicyQuote has an attribute of type WfCovAddress, which in turn has an attribute of type WfCovGeoPoint; and an attribute 'Items' of type 'WfCovCoverageItem List', which makes the kernel ask the IESpace for the LIST TYPE inside the declaration of the structure itself. Then a server action receives a record AND a list of records as INPUT, returns a record as OUTPUT, reads the nesting by the full path and APPENDS to the list that lives inside the output record (ListAppend with Quote.Items). In ODC everything that the public (shareable) action touches has to be shareable, so the four structures are born public - and being public is also what stops them from being born with UnusedElement.

expectedMessages.why: ODC: an app (CrossDevice) does not expose a public server action (the live Studio gives an error); the action stays private and without a consumer in this proof job

ops._why: ONE op declares the four structures: the compiler declares all the types BEFORE the fields, so an attribute can cite a structure declared further down in the same block and the nesting does not require separate deliveries (the same rule as circular entity FKs)

ops._why: STRUCTURE AS A PARAMETER (record): the whole input is a composite type, and it already carries a nested level of its own (Geo)

STRUCTURE LIST AS A PARAMETER: the list type already exists because the structure WfCovPolicyQuote requested it in the attribute Items; here it is proven that the same type serves as an input contract
STRUCTURE AS AN OUTPUT: a single output carries the whole nesting - it is exactly the shape of a REST JSON body
whole record into a record: the Address attribute of the output receives the Address parameter in one go, without copying field by field (and takes the Geo along)

NESTED read by the full path on the RIGHT side: Quote.Address.Zone crosses output -> structure -> attribute. It reads from Quote (already filled in by the previous assignment, which runs first) to prove that the nesting is navigable after being written

THREE LEVELS from the PARAMETER: parameter -> WfCovAddress -> WfCovGeoPoint -> Latitude. It is the same shape as 'GetLatest.Response.Rates.USD' of rest-query-nested.json in SS11, here without going through REST
loop over the STRUCTURE LIST received as a parameter: CoverLines.Current.<Attribute> is read, WITHOUT the aggregate level (there is no aggregate in this job)
accumulates by reading the current element of the structure list of the parameter
in ODC the ListAppend exists as IClientActionSignature AND as IServerActionSignature; inside a server action the IExecuteServerActionNode only accepts the server one

the point of the job: the list being appended to is NOT a loose variable, it is the list attribute that lives INSIDE the output record. Writing Quote.Items proves that the nested structure list is a writable destination like any other
element = the current record of the list parameter, passed whole
